name: αἱ φύσεις
roots: φύσις (from φύω, to grow, to be born); τί (something: the Stoics' highest genus, divided into σώματα, bodies, and ἀσώματα, incorporeals — the λεκτόν among them)

name: σῶμα
roots: σῶμα (in Homer the corpse, later every body; for the Stoics what alone exists, acting or acted upon); τὸ τριχῇ διαστατόν (extended three ways: length, breadth, depth — Diogenes Laertius 7.135)

name: λεκτόν
roots: λέγω (first to gather, to pick out, to lay in order, and so to count and to say — the verb of λόγος); the Stoics' incorporeal that subsists (ὑφίσταται) and does not exist as a body does: what a sentence says

name: φύσις
roots: φύω (to grow, to be born)

name: γένος
roots: γίγνομαι (to come to be, to be born): a kind is a line of what comes to be alike; Aristotle's γένος (genus) above εἶδος (species)

name: τὰ γένη
roots: γένος (a kind), γίγνομαι (to come to be)

name: ἡ τάξις τῶν σωμάτων
roots: τάξις (an arrangement, a rank in battle, from τάσσω, to array); Aristotle, History of Animals 588b: nature passes little by little from the lifeless to the living

name: στοιχειῶδες σωμάτιον
roots: στοιχεῖον (a member of a row; a letter; Plato's and Aristotle's element); σωμάτιον (a little body); τὰ ἐλάχιστα (Epicurus: the least parts, themselves without parts) — the Modern Greek word, in the ancient form

name: ἁδρόνιον
roots: ἁδρός (thick, strong, full-grown) — the Modern Greek word, in the ancient form

name: πυρήν
roots: πυρήν (the stone of a fruit; Modern Greek's nucleus)

name: ἄτομον
roots: ἀ- (not) + τέμνω (to cut): the uncut; Leucippus and Democritus: ἄτομα καὶ κενόν, atoms and void

name: μόριον
roots: μόριον (a part, a portion — Aristotle's word for the parts of animals; Modern Greek's molecule); μοῖρα (a share)

name: κύτταρον
roots: κύτταρος (the cell of a honeycomb, in Aristotle); κύτος (a hollow, a vessel)

name: ἱστός
roots: ἱστός (the web on a loom; the mast, what stands upright — hence histology); ὑφή (a weave)

name: ὄργανον
roots: ἔργον (work); Aristotle, De Anima II.1: the soul is the first actuality of a natural body that has organs (σώματος φυσικοῦ ὀργανικοῦ)

name: σύστημα ὀργάνων
roots: σύστημα (a whole standing together, from συνίστημι); ὄργανον

name: σῶμα ἔμψυχον
roots: ψυχή (breath, life); ἔμψυχος (ensouled, alive); Aristotle: the living body is σῶμα φυσικὸν ὀργανικόν, a natural body with organs

name: πληθυσμός
roots: πλῆθος (a multitude, a throng); ἀγέλη (a herd: Aristotle's gregarious animals, ἀγελαῖα) — the Modern Greek word, in the ancient form

name: κοινωνία
roots: κοινός (common); Aristotle's κοινωνία: every partnership of the living, the city among them

name: οἰκοσύστημα
roots: οἶκος (a house, a household); σύστημα — the Modern Greek word, in the ancient form

name: βιόσφαιρα
roots: βίος (a lived life — beside ζωή, life as such); σφαῖρα — the Modern Greek word, in the ancient form

name: ὕλη
roots: ὕλη (wood, timber, a forest — Aristotle's matter): the same image as materia

name: πέτρα
roots: πέτρα (a rock, a cliff); λίθος (a stone)

name: οὐράνιον σῶμα
roots: οὐρανός (the sky, heaven); Aristotle's heavenly bodies, of the fifth body, αἰθήρ

name: ἐξάρτημα
roots: ἐξαρτάω (to hang from, to fit on); ἐξαρτίζω (to fit out, as a ship is); μέρος (a part)

name: μηχανή
roots: μηχανή (a contrivance, a means, from μῆχος, a remedy, a way); ὄργανον (a tool)

name: κατασκευή
roots: κατασκευάζω (to equip fully, to build, to furnish): a construction, an establishment

name: στέφανος
roots: στέφω (to encircle, to wreathe)

name: θεός
roots: θεός; τὸ ἕν (the One: Plotinus, Enneads VI.9 — the source of all, and itself none of the things it is the source of)

name: ἀγάπη
roots: ἀγαπάω (to welcome, to cherish, to be content with); beside ἔρως (desire) and φιλία (friendship); 1 Corinthians 13:5: οὐ ζητεῖ τὰ ἑαυτῆς, it seeks not its own

name: ποιητής
roots: ποιέω (to make — the maker, and the poet); δημιουργός (a worker for the people: Plato's maker of the cosmos); ζωοποιός (life-making)

name: κατάστασις
roots: καθίστημι (to set down, to establish); στάσις (a standing)

name: διαστάσεις
roots: διΐστημι (to set apart); the Stoics' body is τριχῇ διαστατόν, extended three ways

name: χρόνος
roots: χρόνος (a span of time); for the Stoics one of the four incorporeals, with τόπος (place), κενόν (void) and λεκτόν

name: μῆκος
roots: μῆκος (length; also height, greatness); διάστημα (an interval)

name: πότε
roots: πότε (when: one of Aristotle's ten categories, Categories 1b26)

name: ποῦ
roots: ποῦ (where: the category); τόπος (place: for the Stoics an incorporeal, what a body occupies)

name: τὰ συμπληρώματα
roots: συμπληρόω (to fill up together); πλήρης (full)

name: ῥητόν
roots: ῥητός (stated, said expressly — and in mathematics, rational, what has a stated ratio)

name: ὁ φέρων
roots: φέρω (to bear); ὑποκείμενον (what lies under and bears)

name: σύστημα
roots: συνίστημι (to set together)

name: διαίρεσις
roots: διαιρέω (to take apart); Plato, Phaedrus 265e: to cut where the natural joints are (κατ' ἄρθρα ᾗ πέφυκεν); στιγμή (a point, a prick)

name: αἱ διαιρέσεις
roots: διαιρέω (to take apart)

name: μέρος
roots: μέρος (a part, a share, from μείρομαι, to receive one's portion); ὅλον (the whole)

name: οἰκεῖ ἐν
roots: οἰκέω (to dwell); οἶκος (a house)

name: κεῖται ἐν
roots: κεῖμαι (to lie: Aristotle's category κεῖσθαι, position); τόπος (a place); θέσις (a placing)

name: ὁ κεκτημένος
roots: κτάομαι (to acquire): the possessor; κτῆμα (a possession)

name: ὑπεύθυνος
roots: εὐθύνη (the account an Athenian official gave at the end of office): liable to give account

name: πράξεις
roots: πράσσω (to do, to pass through)

name: ποιηθέν
roots: ποιέω (to make — the root of poetry)

name: παράγωγον
roots: παράγω (to lead aside, to bring forth); the grammarians' παράγωγος (a word formed from another)

name: ἀναγνωσθέν
roots: ἀναγιγνώσκω (to know again, to recognise: to read)

name: λεχθέν
roots: λέγω (to say — the verb of λεκτόν); ῥῆμα (a thing said)

name: προέλευσις
roots: προέρχομαι (to come forth); μαρτυρία (a testimony)

name: στρώματα
roots: στρώννυμι (to spread): a layer spread upon another

name: ἐπαγγελία
roots: ἀγγέλλω (to announce): a public declaration — and a promise

name: νόμος
roots: νέμω (to distribute, to allot: a law is an allotment); θεσμός (what is laid down, from τίθημι)

name: αἰτιολογία
roots: αἰτία (a cause, a charge) + λόγος (an account): the giving of causes

name: ἐφημερίδες
roots: ἐφ' ἡμέρᾳ (upon the day): the day-journals, as Alexander's court kept; διφθέρα (a prepared hide: the writing stuff that gave daftar its name)

name: ἱστορία
roots: ἵστωρ (one who knows by having seen: a witness, a judge)

name: τὰ ἐκκρεμῆ
roots: ἐκκρεμής (hanging from, in suspense): what still hangs undecided

name: ὀνόματα
roots: ὄνομα (a name); Plato's Cratylus: whether names are by nature (φύσει) or by convention (θέσει) — here by convention, for a reader

name: ὄψις
roots: ὄψομαι (I shall see): a sight, an appearance; θέα (a spectacle)

name: φακοί
roots: φακός (a lentil — and the lens)

name: ἀνατολή
roots: ἀνατέλλω (to rise, as the sun): the rising, the east

name: σύνεσις
roots: συνίημι (to send together, to bring together: to see how parts go together)

name: ἐνέργεια
roots: ἐν + ἔργον (at work): Aristotle's being-at-work — what is at work now

name: ἐξέτασις
roots: ἐξετάζω (to examine closely, to test — Apology 38a: ὁ ἀνεξέταστος βίος, the unexamined life)

name: κῆπος
roots: κῆπος (a garden: Epicurus's school); παράδεισος (from Persian pairi-daēza: Xenophon's word for the Persian king's walled parks)

name: ὄνομα
roots: ὄνομα (a name)
